description_summary: 12-month unduplicated enrollment counts are broken down by student level and degree/certificate-seeking status, with undergraduate detail for full-time versus part-time attendance and, among degree/certificate-seeking students, first-time, transfer-in, and continuing status. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and EFFYALEV, and contains totals by men/women and race/ethnicity; other-gender counts are available only for total undergraduate and graduate levels, not the detailed undergraduate categories or attendance statuses.

12-month unduplicated enrollment counts are broken down by student level and distance-education status. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and EFFYDLEV and reports total enrollment plus students enrolled exclusively in distance education, in some distance education, or in none.

12-month unduplicated counts cover high-school students enrolled in college courses for credit, a subset of nondegree/non-certificate-seeking enrollment, and are broken down by gender and race/ethnicity. Each record is identified by UNITID and contains total, men, and women counts, including the nine race/ethnicity categories; it does not represent all undergraduate enrollment.

12-month instructional activity totals hold credit-hour and/or contact-hour measures for undergraduate and graduate instruction, used to represent institution-level instructional activity and derive 12-month FTE enrollment. The relevant grain is institution by instructional level rather than an unduplicated student headcount.

Institution-level academic library data for fiscal year 2023, covering library characteristics, collections, expenditures, services, and full-time-equivalent library staff. The table applies only to degree-granting institutions; expenditure data are available for institutions with total expenditures over $100,000. Full-time-equivalent staff have been collected since fiscal year 2020, and physical versus electronic serial collections have been distinguished since fiscal year 2016–17. The Academic Libraries survey has been part of IPEDS since collection year 2014–15.

Institution-level counts and indicators for undergraduate admission considerations, applicants, admitted applicants, enrolled admitted students, and SAT/ACT scores among entering first-time, degree- or certificate-seeking students. The table applies only to institutions without an open-admissions policy for entering first-time students; SAT and ACT measures apply where test scores are required for admission. It includes additional gender categories for students outside the men/women categories; in 2023–24, another-gender values below five students were not reported.

Awards and degrees conferred by six-digit 2020 CIP program, award level, first or second major, race/ethnicity, and gender. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID, CIPCODE, MAJORNUM, and AWLEVEL; award-level fields distinguish certificates of less than 12 weeks from certificates of at least 12 weeks but less than 1 year.

Students receiving any awards or degrees, broken down by race/ethnicity and gender. Each institution has one record uniquely identified by UNITID; additional nonbinary/other-gender variables are available only for total undergraduate and total graduate students.

Students receiving awards or degrees by award level, race/ethnicity, gender, and age group. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and AWLEVEL; age counts are provided for under 18, 18–24, 25–39, and 40 or older, but race, gender, and age cannot be cross-tabulated together. Award-level fields distinguish certificates of less than 12 weeks from certificates of at least 12 weeks but less than 1 year.

Programs offered and programs whose programs can be completed entirely via distance education, by six-digit CIP program and award level. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and CIPCODE: six-digit CIP records indicate which award levels are offered, which have all programs available entirely by distance education, and which have some programs available entirely by distance education; two-digit CIP records summarize the number of six-digit programs, and CIPCODE 99 provides institution totals.

Fall enrollment counts broken down by gender, full- or part-time attendance status, and student level. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID, attendance status, and student level (EFLEVEL), and includes total, men’s, and women’s counts.

Fall enrollment counts broken down by race/ethnicity, gender, full- or part-time attendance status, and student level. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID, attendance status, and student level (EFALEVEL); race/ethnicity categories and men’s and women’s counts are included, with other-gender variables available for total undergraduate and graduate levels beginning in fall 2022. In fall 2023, other-gender values below 5 were not reported when nonzero, and the data are not disaggregated by detailed undergraduate level or attendance status for those variables.

Fall enrollment counts broken down by distance-education status and student level. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and student level (EFDELEV), and includes total enrollment plus counts enrolled exclusively, partly, or not at all in distance education; exclusive-distance-education counts are further broken down by the student’s location relative to the institution, including same state, different state, U.S. state unknown, and outside the U.S.

Fall enrollment counts broken down by age category, gender, full- or part-time attendance status, and student level. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID, age category (EFBAGE), and student level (LSTUDY). Age reporting is optional in even-numbered years, so 2023 (odd) has data under the catalog’s rule.

First-time freshman counts broken down by state of residence, including counts who graduated from high school the previous year. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and state of residence (EFCSTATE). Residence reporting is optional in odd-numbered years, so 2023 (odd) is an optional reporting year and data may be absent for institutions that did not report.

Institution-level measures of total entering class, first-year retention rate, and student-to-faculty ratio; the grain is one record per UNITID. The measures apply only to institutions with undergraduate students. Entering-class data are reported only by academic-year institutions, and short-program institutions of less than one year do not have retention data.

Institution-level finance records for public institutions using GASB 34/35, keyed by UNITID, covering revenues by source, expenditures by functional and natural classification, endowments, assets and liabilities, and financial health measures. This is the GASB form, including public institutions rather than FASB-reporting institutions.

Institution-level finance records keyed by UNITID for all private not-for-profit institutions and public institutions that use FASB accounting standards. It contains revenues, functional and natural expenditures, endowments, assets and liabilities, and financial health measures.

Institution-level finance records keyed by UNITID for private for-profit institutions using FASB accounting standards. It contains revenues, functional and natural expenditures, assets and liabilities, and financial health measures, but not the endowment data included in the other finance forms.

100%-, 150%-, and 200%-of-normal-time completion outcomes for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates, with records identified by UNITID and the applicable cohort/status code. It covers four-year institutions’ 2015 cohorts for bachelor’s completion and less-than-four-year institutions’ 2019 cohorts for completion of any degree or certificate.

150%-of-normal-time graduation and transfer outcomes for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates, with records identified by UNITID and cohort/status code GRTYPE and results reported by gender and race/ethnicity. It covers four-year institutions’ 2017 cohorts and two-year institutions’ 2020 cohorts, including bachelor’s and other credential-seeking groups where applicable; 100%-of-normal-time completion counts are not available jointly by gender and race/ethnicity for two-year institutions.

Counts of students in revised graduation-rate cohorts whose gender is not reported as men or women, identified by UNITID and the applicable revised-cohort/status code. It covers the 2017 four-year and 2020 less-than-four-year cohorts and contains no completion outcomes.

100%- and 150%-of-normal-time completion and transfer outcomes for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates at less-than-two-year institutions, identified at the institution/cohort level by UNITID and the applicable cohort or status code. It covers the 2020 cohort and contains no gender, race/ethnicity, or financial-aid subcohort breakdown.

150%-of-normal-time completion outcomes for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates split into three financial-aid subcohorts: Pell Grant recipients, Direct Subsidized Loan recipients who did not receive Pell, and students who received neither; records are identified by UNITID and PSGRTYPE. It includes four-year institutions’ 2017 cohorts and two-year and less-than-two-year institutions’ 2020 cohorts, with bachelor’s and other credential-seeking groups reported where applicable.

Staff counts broken down by full- or part-time status, medical-school status, occupational category, faculty/tenure status, and, for non-tenure-track staff, contract length. Each row is uniquely identified by UNITID and EAPCAT; multi-year and indefinite contract categories are available from 2016 onward.

Full-time instructional staff counts at degree-granting institutions with 15 or more full-time employees and related administrative offices, broken down by faculty/tenure status, academic rank, race/ethnicity, and gender, with non-tenure-track contract length also available. Each row is uniquely identified by UNITID and SISCAT; race/ethnicity and gender reporting is mandatory annually from 2016 onward, so 2023 has data, and multi-year and indefinite contract categories are available from 2016 onward.

Full-time new hires at degree-granting institutions with 15 or more full-time employees and related administrative offices, broken down by primary occupation, race/ethnicity, and gender; instructional new hires also have faculty/tenure status and, from 2016 onward, non-tenure-track contract length. The new-hire period is November 1, 2022 through October 31, 2023, and each row is uniquely identified by UNITID and SNHCAT; race/ethnicity and gender reporting is mandatory annually from 2016 onward, so 2023 has data.

Full- and part-time staff counts on the November 1 payroll, broken down by occupational category, race/ethnicity, and gender. Each row is uniquely identified by UNITID and STAFFCAT; race/ethnicity and gender reporting is mandatory annually from 2016 onward, so 2023 has data.

Full-time instructional staff counts at degree-granting institutions with 15 or more full-time employees and related administrative offices, broken down by academic rank, faculty/tenure status, and non-tenure-track contract length. Each row is uniquely identified by UNITID and FACSTAT; multi-year and indefinite contract categories are available from 2016 onward.

Counts, salary outlays, average salaries, and equated 9-month salary measures for full-time nonmedical instructional staff, broken down by academic rank, gender, and number of months worked. Each row is keyed by UNITID and ARANK; staff working less than 9 months are counted but have no salary fields.
Counts and salary outlays for full-time, nonmedical, noninstructional staff by occupational category.

Custom comparison-group membership records for the 2024 IPEDS Data Feedback Report. Each row identifies a comparison institution by its UNITID, name, and state within a submitted group; the row grain is the submitting institution/group and comparison institution.

Institution-by-survey-component response-status records keyed by UNITID and survey component. The rows identify response, imputation, applicability, parent/child multi-campus reporting, and—where applicable in final or revised releases—submission of revised data.

Institution-level directory and classification records keyed by UNITID, containing names, addresses, institutional URLs, active-status and Title IV participation indicators, plus control, institutional level, highest offering and degree, and Carnegie classification variables.

Institution-level records keyed by UNITID covering educational offerings and award levels, organization and affiliations, admissions policy, special learning opportunities, distance education, library services, and athletic associations. Beginning in 2020-21, less-than-one-year certificates are separated into less-than-12-weeks and at-least-12-weeks-but-less-than-one-year categories; selected admissions-related fields are updated from winter admissions data.

Institution-level academic-year charge records keyed by UNITID for institutions with primarily credit-hour academic programs using semester, quarter, trimester, 4-1-4, or another academic calendar. The table contains full-time undergraduate and graduate tuition and required fees, part-time per-credit charges, charges for specified professional-practice programs, and published attendance prices for full-time first-time undergraduates, including tuition, fees, books, supplies, room and board, and other expenses.

Branch-location records keyed by the reporting main-campus institution and branch location, containing branch names, addresses, URLs, institutional-level and award-offering variables, and cost-of-attendance fields where the branch enrolls full-time first-time undergraduates. This is an optional, noncomprehensive list of branch locations reported for College Navigator, not a census of all Title IV branches.

Institution-level records keyed by UNITID for institutions using clock hours or primarily occupational credit-hour programs, reporting charges for the full length of vocational programs rather than an academic year. Fields cover the number of programs, attendance price for the largest program, and tuition, fees, and books and supplies for up to five additional programs.
Institution-level mission records keyed by UNITID containing either the institution’s mission statement or the web address where it is provided.

Award and enrollment outcomes for degree- and certificate-seeking undergraduates who entered during July 1, 2015–June 30, 2016, measured at four years (August 31, 2019), six years (August 31, 2021), and eight years (August 31, 2023). The population is reported by four entry-status cohorts—first-time full-time, first-time part-time, non-first-time full-time, and non-first-time part-time—each split into Pell recipients and non-Pell recipients. Records are uniquely identified by IPEDS ID (UNITID) and cohort (OMCHRT), and contain revised and adjusted cohort sizes plus counts and percentages completing or still enrolled; the table covers degree-granting institutions and excludes undergraduates outside the degree/certificate-seeking entering cohorts.

Undergraduate student financial aid recipients and aid amounts broken down by student population, aid source, and aid type. The row grain is institution × undergraduate population/status × aid category, covering full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates and all undergraduates, with degree/certificate-seeking and non-degree/non-certificate-seeking groups distinguished where applicable; variables include recipient counts, total aid dollars, and average aid dollars. Federal grants, Pell grants, state/local grants, institutional grants, and federal and nonfederal loans are reported for the first-time cohort, while all-undergraduate measures include total grants, Pell grants, and federal loans, with non-degree/non-certificate-seeking undergraduate Pell and federal-loan measures available for 2022-23.

Average net price and its underlying financial-aid amounts for two groups of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates: those receiving grant or scholarship aid and those receiving Title IV federal student aid. The row grain is institution × aid-recipient group; at public institutions, both groups are restricted to students paying in-district or in-state tuition.

Military, servicemember, and veteran benefit recipients and benefit amounts broken down by benefit program and student level. The row grain is institution × undergraduate/graduate student level × benefit type, covering Post-9/11 GI Bill benefits and the Department of Defense Tuition Assistance Program, with recipient counts and total dollars received through the institution.
